wc.heading: Primary Working Capital
wc.text:
We use primary working capital ("PWC") as a percentage of sales as a key metric for working capital efficiency. We define this metric as the sum of receivables and inventories less payables, divided by the last 12 months net sales. As of December 31, 2024, the Company classified the short term portion of deferred revenue as other current liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheet, whereas previously short term deferred revenue was included in payables. The following table shows the components of our PWC:

Overall, PWC increased $16.7 million compared to the previous year-end. Receivables at December 31, 2024 were $84.3 million compared to $83.5 million at the end of 2023, an increase of $0.8 million due to increased sales, offset by improved days sales outstanding. The Company believes its receivables balance is fully collectible. Inventories at December 31, 2024 were $143.4 million compared to $153.7 million at the end of 2023. Inventory decreased $10.2 million, due to effective inventory management. Payables at December 31, 2024 were $55.7 million compared to $81.8 million at the end of 2023. The decrease was due to the short term deferred revenue being classified in other current liabilities, lower inventory balance and the timing of payments relative to year end.

The increase in utility water sales reflected strong growth across the Company's broad suite of smart water solutions, led by cellular AMI adoption, including mechanical and ultrasonic meters, ORION Cellular endpoints, and BEACON SaaS revenues. Sales of products into the global flow instrumentation end markets were $101.1 million, 0.6% higher than the prior year’s $100.5 million due to modest growth across the water-focused end markets, offset by slight declines in de-emphasized general industrial markets.

Net sales in 2023 increased $138.0 million, or 24.4%, to $703.6 million from $565.6 million in 2022. Sales into the utility water market were $603.1 million, an increase of 27.8% over the prior year’s $471.8 million. The increase in utility water sales reflected strong growth across the Company's broad suite of smart water solutions and the continued robust adoption of cellular AMI solutions, specifically ORION Cellular endpoints and BEACON SaaS revenues, as well as increased E-Series Ultrasonic meter volumes.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: With more than a century of water technology innovation, Badger Meter is a global provider of industry leading water management solutions, with approximately 95% of net sales derived from water-related applications.
No single customer accounts for more than 10% of the Company's sales.

The Company’s net sales and corresponding net earnings depend on unit volume and product mix, with the Company generally earning higher average selling prices and margins on meters coupled with radio technology, software, water quality monitoring, sewer line and lift station monitoring and on ultrasonic compared to mechanical meters.
There are multiple sources for these raw materials and components, but the Company relies on single suppliers for certain brass castings, resins and electronic subassemblies.
We rely on our agreements with customers, confidentiality agreements with employees, and our trademarks, trade secrets, copyrights and patents to protect our proprietary rights.

In addition, we rely on single suppliers for microprocessors, castings and components in several of our product lines and the loss of such suppliers could temporarily disrupt operations in the short term.
Our operations rely on favorable trade relations between the U.S. and those foreign countries in which we and our customers and our suppliers have operations.
Our success depends on our continued ability to identify, attract, develop and retain skilled personnel throughout our organization.
The main sources of liquidity for the Company are cash from operations and borrowing capacity.
These factors are largely beyond the Company's control and depend on the economic condition and regulatory environment of the geographic region of the Company's operations.
The Company relies on single suppliers for certain castings and components in several of its product lines.

The Company attempts to mitigate these risks by working closely with key suppliers, purchasing minimal amounts from alternative suppliers and by purchasing business interruption insurance where appropriate.
The Company relies on single suppliers for most brass castings and certain resin and electronic subassemblies in several of its product lines.
